newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss fund assets seen at 2.0 trillion Sfr by 2000.
newsitem.headline: Swiss fund assets seen at 2.0 trillion Sfr by 2000.

text.p: Swiss institutional investors are expected to have 2.0 trillion Swiss francs under management worldwide by the year 2000, more than double the current Swiss bourse capitalisation, according to a new study published by Bank Julius Baer.
According to Baer analyst Hans Kaufmann, author of the study, "the collective investments in recent years have taken on massive significance."
The study said growth has been vigorous in the past few years, even though 1994 was one of the worst years for investment returns in recent memory.

Baer said the increases in the amount of money managed were augmented by acquisitions in the insurance industry and by banks' increased activities in this area. Investments were seen growing at a rate of 100 billion francs per annum over roughly the next two years.

Baer also estimated total assets under management by the seven major investment groups -- government pension funds and accident insurance funds, occupational and company pension funds, private insurers, banks, private investment funds, investment societies, and industrial concerns -- at 1.224 trillion francs at end-1995.

Banks alone are seen as having securities holdings at the end of 1995 of roughly 250 billion Swiss francs including investments of foreign subsidiaries, "although only a portion of that is actually exposed to market risk," Baer said. It said a significant amount was tied up in derivatives activities, securities lending and similar activities.
"But it is still notable that the amount of securities relative to the balance sheet total ... has risen from 10 percent to 16 percent, and this trend will continue," Baer said.
Swiss insurers' invested assets totalled an estimated 350 billion francs under management at end-1995, including foreign subsidiaries, and 254 billion francs for Swiss operations alone.
Their domestic investments in equities, excluding insurance stocks, rose to 33.2 billion francs or 12 percent of total holdings at end-1995 from nine percent in 1992, Baer said.

The 10 largest Swiss insurers alone were seen with 319.5 billion francs invested on a worldwide basis. Roughly half of that, or 159 billion francs, is held in bonds, and only 46.8 billion francs or 15 percent in equities.
The second-largest contingent of funds under management, held by roughly 12,800 company and occupational pension funds, was estimated at 315 billion Swiss francs at the end of 1995.
In dollar terms, the amount was estimated at $280 billion, and is forecast to grow to as much as $501 billion according to some calculations by the year 2000, Baer said.
It said that by the end of 1994, the pension fund assets were already equal to roughly 83 percent of Swiss GDP.

Pension funds held roughly 40.2 billion Swiss francs in equities at the end of 1994, an amount equal to 14 percent of total assets. The amount has increased by 19.5 percent from 1984 to 1994. The funds could also place more money outside Switzerland in the future, Baer said.
"The geographic diversification of the pension funds' assets could continue to increase, with foreign shares also coming under consideration," Baer said.
At the same time, Baer expected foreign pension funds to place more money in Swiss securities markets, a factor which would tend to offset the outflow from domestic funds.
